extraction.name: LongVid
extraction.description: A large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset comprising 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering pairs across five task types for diverse long video scenarios.
extraction.creator: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, Limin Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongVid was built by leveraging existing datasets and curating long videos with dense event labels, then constructing QA pairs from captions, event labels, and timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing datasets including Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-Vila, and MiraData; captions and event-level annotations from Panda-70M, CosMo, Ego4D-HCap, HT-Step, and MiraData.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors filtered consecutive segments that could be regrouped into long video sequences and constructed event label sequences with timestamps; for some datasets they directly used event-level annotations, and for others they extracted major events from captions using an LLM.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Dense event labels were generated for each long video, and long video QA pairs were constructed from video captions, event labels, and timestamps. Task categories were video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing long-form video-text datasets lack the instruction-following paradigm crucial for multimodal reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Long video instruction tuning and supporting models to handle diverse long video scenarios across five tasks: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.

name.evidence: Second, to further enrich the existing long video training corpus, we construct LongVid, a dataset that contains 300,000 hours of videos and 2 billion words of textual annotations.

description.evidence: To address this, we introduce a large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset named LongVid. It comprises 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering (QA) pairs across five different task types, supporting models to handle diverse long video scenarios.

inLanguage.evidence: To address this, we introduce a large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset named LongVid. It comprises 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering (QA) pairs across five different task types, supporting models to handle diverse long video scenarios.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: To build LongVid, we leverages the rich diversity of existing datasets, including Ego4D [19], HowTo100M [37], HD-Vila [62], and MiraData [22], encompassing a wide range of video types: movies, egocentric videos, news, interviews, and how-to videos, and other in-the-wild videos of long duration. For data curation, we generate dense event labels for each long video.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: To build LongVid, we leverages the rich diversity of existing datasets, including Ego4D [19], HowTo100M [37], HD-Vila [62], and MiraData [22]... Finally, we construct several types of long video QA pairs based on the video captions, event labels, and the timestamps of short video segments.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: To build LongVid, we leverages the rich diversity of existing datasets, including Ego4D [19], HowTo100M [37], HD-Vila [62], and MiraData [22]... Specifically, we utilize existing high-quality short video captions (Panda-70M [11] for HD-VILA [62], CosMo [51] for HowTo100M [37], Ego4D-HCap [21] for Ego4D [19], and the original high-quality captions provided in MiraData [22])

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Specifically, we utilize existing high-quality short video captions ... and filter the consecutive segments that can be regroup into a long video sequence, then we construct a sequence of event labels with their corresponding timestamps for every long video based on their captions. In this process, for datasets with high-quality event-level annotations ... we directly utilize them as the event labels, while for others, we extract the major event from the caption using an LLM.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: For data curation, we generate dense event labels for each long video... Finally, we construct several types of long video QA pairs based on the video captions, event labels, and the timestamps of short video segments. They are categorized into five tasks: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: for others, we extract the major event from the caption using an LLM.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Though recent advances have mitigated this by long-form datasets of video-text pairs, these lack the instruction-following paradigm, such as (video, instruction, answer) triplets, crucial for multimodal reasoning.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: To address this, we introduce a large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset named LongVid. It comprises 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering (QA) pairs across five different task types, supporting models to handle diverse long video scenarios... They are categorized into five tasks: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.
